definition: Information that does not follow a fixed schema, such as text, documents, images, audio and video.
details: Most enterprise data is unstructured and historically hard for software to query. Embeddings and vector search changed that by turning raw documents into comparable numerical representations, making the data searchable by meaning rather than exact keywords.

explainer.lead: Unstructured data is information with no fixed schema — text, documents, images, audio and video. It makes up most enterprise data, so making it queryable is a major practical problem.

tiers.eli5: Most of an organisation's information is like a pile of photos and letters rather than a neat spreadsheet, so a computer can't just look things up by column.
tiers.practitioner: Embeddings turn raw documents into vectors so you can search by meaning instead of exact keywords. Pitfall: chunking and embedding quality decide retrieval quality — garbage in, garbage retrieved.
tiers.paperLevel: Data whose records do not conform to a predefined schema; historically unqueryable by relational methods, now handled by mapping items to comparable numerical representations and using vector search.

explainer.example: A company embeds thousands of PDF policy documents and retrieves the relevant passages for a question by nearest-vector search rather than keyword matching.
